children: By Stephen Culp and Shashwat Chauhan

Wall Street stocks slightly pared gains after the US Federal Reserve left its key policy rate unchanged, as widely expected, shifting the probability of a rate hike to its next monetary policy meeting in December.
In its accompanying statement, the Fed upgraded its assessment of the economy while acknowledging inflation "remains elevated."
"The Fed didn't throw any curveballs," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. "It was widely expected they'd hold, so no big surprise there."
"Likely the pressure will be to do one more hike in December, as inflation is still potentially an issue," Detrick added.
Investors' focus now turns to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference, which they will scrutinize for clues regarding the central bank's path through the end of the year and into 2027.

Of the three major US stock indexes, which were muted and directionless before the Fed's announcement, the S&P 500 and the Dow were slightly higher, while the Nasdaq moved nominally lower. Warsh's press conference is set to begin at 2:30 p.m. ET (1830 GMT).
Financial markets are pricing in an 86.0% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, up from 78.3% on Tuesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Rate hike forecasts could be swayed by upcoming data expected on Thursday, including the Commerce Department's Personal Consumption Expenditures report, which includes the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, and an advance take on third-quarter GDP.
